what_happened: After handoff the ego, going about 12 m/s in the right lane with the route continuing straight and then right, steered left into the adjacent lane and hit the front of car 2, which was ahead in that lane, without braking. The ego was 1.5 m off the recorded path when it hit.

After handoff the policy kept about 12 m/s and drifted left out of its lane into the next lane, which the recorded human did not do (the human path stays right, and the command turns RIGHT). It ran its front into the silver car (actor 2) driving in that lane and never braked meaningfully.

On a straight multi-lane road, the policy took over and drifted left out of its lane toward the adjacent lane, while the recorded human path stayed right. Holding about 12 m/s with no braking, it cut in close behind/beside actor 2 in that lane and hit it with its front.

After handoff the ego held about 12 m/s and drifted left into the next lane, while the recorded route went straight and then right. That put it right behind the slower actor 2. The gap to actor 2 fell from 27.6 m to 4.5 m in half a second, and the ego hit its rear with almost no braking.

After handoff, the ego held about 12 m/s and veered left into the next lane instead of following the recorded path, which stays right (the command changes to RIGHT). Its front hit car 2, a slower vehicle in that lane, without braking. The gap to car 2 fell from 27.6 m to 4.5 m in the last half second.

On a RIGHT command, the ego made a tight, slow right turn (about 3.5 m/s) that drifted almost 8 m off the recorded path toward the curb and the parked cars on the new street. Its front hit vehicle 112, which was turning into the same street just ahead and to its side (gap 4.1 m at 9.6 s), and the ego also left the drivable area at the corner.

While making the commanded right turn at the intersection, the ego turned much more sharply than the recorded human path. By 9.6 s it was pointing almost straight at the curb and drove front-first into the parked cars along the curb (actors 90/16), about 7.5 m off the recorded path.

On the commanded right turn, the ego turned far too tightly at about 3.5 m/s and left the recorded path by about 8 m. It headed across the lane toward the curb and hit a car parked there (actor 90/119 area) with its front. By 10.1 s the camera shows the ego pointed straight at the sidewalk and a brick wall.

With a RIGHT command at the intersection, the ego turned too wide and too sharply at about 3–4 m/s. It ran across the travel lane into the curbside parking lane and hit parked car 90 with its front, ending 7.6 m from the recorded human path. Its own planned path (orange) pointed into the row of parked cars the whole time.

On the RIGHT command, the ego turned right at the intersection. It cut the turn tighter than the human path and sped up from 3.2 to 4.0 m/s, and its front hit parked car 90 at the curb of the cross street, about 6.8 m off the recorded trajectory. Car 112, which was crossing behind, also touched the ego's rear, and the run was flagged offroad as the ego went into the curb-side parking area.

The route said RIGHT, but the ego went straight and drifted slightly left into the path of the white sedan (actor 99), which was braking to a near stop ahead of it before the intersection. The ego only eased from about 13 to 10 m/s while the gap shrank from 34 m to 0.5 m, so it hit the sedan with its front. It was rear-ended only after that.

After handoff the ego was going straight at about 9.5 m/s. Its path bent left toward the next lane while it crossed the intersection, so it moved into that lane and hit actor 33, which was driving next to it on the left. The lead vehicle stayed about 18 m ahead, and the camera view looked clean until the moment of impact.

The route turns right at the intersection, but after handoff at 4.7s the policy kept planning straight and slightly left, and the ego was flagged offroad at 6.2s as it reached the stop line at about 9 m/s. It was only 0.8 m from the human's path and its box still looks inside the lanes on the map, so the offroad flag may come from the map's road boundary rather than a real departure.

On a RIGHT command, the ego made the turn at about 3–4 m/s but turned too wide and never straightened into the lane like the human did. It ended up nearly crosswise to the new street, about 7 m off the recorded path, and drove its front into parked car 90 at the curb, which also put it off the road.

The route said turn right and the recorded path bore right, but the ego went straight while straddling the lane line to its left. Actor 99, a white sedan that was nearly stopped and partly in the ego's path, was ahead. The gap shrank by about 11 m/s from 34 m to 0.4 m, but the ego only eased off from 12.9 to 10.1 m/s and hit 99's rear corner with its front.

A white car (actor 99) was stopped just ahead of the ego, a little to the left. The ego had drifted about 2 m left of the recorded right-turn path, toward that car. It barely slowed (12.9 to 10.1 m/s) while the gap closed at about 11 m/s, from 34 m to 0.5 m, and its front hit the stopped car at 9.1 s. The rear contact happened later and does not explain the crash.

Approaching the intersection at about 9–10 m/s, the policy's planned path (orange) kept angling left, away from the recorded straight path in its own lane. The ego drifted into the left lane and hit vehicle 33 with its front corner. Vehicle 33 had been driving alongside in that lane.

While approaching the intersection at about 9 m/s, the ego drifted left out of its lane, about 1.3 m off the recorded path. Its front-left corner hit actor 33, which was driving alongside in the left lane. The car ahead was still about 18 m away, so this was not a lead-vehicle crash, and the rear contact came only after this front collision.

While going straight through the intersection at about 9.5 m/s, the ego drifted about 2 m left of the recorded path into the adjacent left lane and ran its front into vehicle 33, which was driving alongside. It never braked, and the 0.6 m gap at the end is vehicle 33 becoming the actor ahead, not a sudden stop by the lead car.

At about 9 m/s, the ego was entering a signalized intersection with a green light, and the policy's plan ran straight ahead. The route, which the command showed as STRAIGHT until the last frame, actually turns right. At 6.2 s the ego was flagged offroad at the intersection entry while only 0.8 m from the recorded human path, and there was no contact with any actor.

The ego was approaching an intersection at about 9 m/s. The route turned right, but the command stayed STRAIGHT until the last frame, and the policy planned straight ahead and slightly left. At the stop line it was flagged offroad, only 0.8 m from where the human drove, with no collision and the lead car about 29 m ahead.

The route turns right at the intersection, but the command showed STRAIGHT until the last frame. After the 4.7 s handoff the policy planned a straight, slightly left-bearing path across the intersection instead of following the right curve. At about 9 m/s the ego's box crossed the drivable-area edge as it entered the intersection. It was only 0.8 m off the human trajectory at that point, so this is a marginal clip, and there was no collision.

The ego was told to keep right but stayed in the left lane, straddling the lane line, behind the white sedan (actor 99), which was slowing toward the intersection. The ego only eased from 13 to 10.4 m/s while the gap fell from 34 m to 0, and its front hit the sedan's rear-right corner.

The route said RIGHT and the recorded path turned right, but the ego kept going straight toward the intersection with its body over the lane line to its left. That put it partly in the path of a white sedan (actor 99), which was slowing ahead of it. The ego only eased off from about 13 to 10 m/s while the gap shrank from 34 m to 0.4 m, and its front hit the sedan at 9.1 s. The rear contact came after this front collision.
